Caelith's Conclusion — Read-Aloud

Read aloud at the start of Scene 7, on the third morning. The evidence is still on the long table; the city is going about its day outside. Caelith judges the party ready to choose how they leave.

Caelith sets the copied countermark beside the clipped coin.

"Cindren and Vhal," he says. "Bonded factors. Respectable enough for clean rooms. Useful enough for dirty ones." He pins the eastern coast to a small map between the squares of linen. "Their house is in Rel Astra, the Old Harbor Ward. The senior partners answer to no one in this kingdom or the next, in any way the law would let us reach them."

Outside, bells ring.

"I do not know whether Haskur Vandrell is there. But someone there was ready for him." He looks at each of you in turn. "And if we have learned this much by morning — then by nightfall they will know we learned it."

Transitions to: Scene 7 · Three Roads East (next page). Caelith now calls the party up to the Old Council Chamber and lays three leather folios on the round table.

GM note. This is the speech that crosses the line. Until now the party has been investigating at home; with this read-aloud, the question pivots from "what happened?" to "how soon do we leave?"

Scene 7 · Three Roads East

The Old Council Chamber. Three folios. Authority, cover, or distance.

After Caelith's conclusion in the Refectory, he calls the party up to the cold, disused Old Council Chamber, where Trina is already seated among the ring of carved chairs. He lays three leather folios on the round table. Three ways east, and — as he says it himself, a finger on each in turn — "I can give you authority, cover, or distance. I cannot give you all three."

Before the folios hit the table — the gate check

Run your gate check first: the five truths from the front of the chapter. The party should leave Loftwick certain that Haskur was kept alive on purpose, that he was a node in a network, that the firm's living hand is in Hardby, that Loftwick won't let them finish here, and that the road runs east and must be taken now. If any of the five is thin, the Quick reference tells you which late line shores it up. Then let them choose their road — and make sure they feel the weight of it, because this choice shapes the next chapter. Speed may save Tamsin; visibility may get her "settled."

Before the folios, say the distance out loud. Hardby is not down the road; it is most of a continent away, and the three folios are three different answers to that fact. Ten weeks, six weeks, or three. They should hear the numbers before they choose.

The Official Delegation (authority)

The party travels as accredited Yeomanry representatives, with credentials, a junior councilman to lend his name, clerks, and a guard escort. It is ten weeks on the road — caravan pace, with a formal stop and a written report at every customs post — and visible the entire way: the firm will know they're coming and roughly when, with a season to sanitize records and move witnesses. They leave in autumn and come into Hardby in the dead of winter. But Aerdi authorities can't touch accredited foreign inquirers, the firm is bound by law to receive them, and any witness they recover can travel home under diplomatic cover.

The slowest road by a wide margin, and the only one that cannot be taken from them.

Commercial Cover (cover — Caelith's quiet recommendation)

By sea. The party goes down the Sheldomar corridor to the Keoish coast and buys passage on a wool trader working east and around into Woolly Bay — as a small wool-buying delegation assessing eastern markets, with real samples in the hold, real letters of introduction, and Trina's letter to the poet Castrian Vell, who keeps an ear in four Hardby salons. Six weeks all in: the ride to the coast, the wait for a hull going the right way, the voyage, and the two ports the master stops at because he is a trader before he is anyone's courier.

It buys plausible access — wool merchants visit counting houses for credit all the time — but it demands discipline, for six weeks in a confined space: anyone who breaks character risks the group, and a paladin in plate or a gnome bard known to the Hardby tavern circuit thins the cover fast. Cargo manifests are filed; passenger lists mostly are not. That is the whole of the cover's protection, and it is thinner than it sounds.

Quiet Pursuit (distance)

The post roads, and a warrant that lets them change horses at every station from the Yeomanry line to the Wild Coast. Caelith can put that warrant in their hands; he cannot make it invisible. Three weeks, which is as fast as a living thing crosses that country, and they will feel every day of it — arrive them saddle-sore, underslept and short-tempered, and let the first Hardby scene be harder for it.

It is not the road that surprises the firm. Nothing surprises the firm; word goes east the day they lean on Vesh and it does not travel by horse. What three weeks buys is arriving before the tidying is finished — while Tamsin is still breathing, the broker is still drinking in the same tavern, and the second set of books is still in the building.

And there is no net: caught east of Hardby with false papers and a bought warrant, the party are just liars to the local watch. Caelith says it plainly — "If you are taken, I cannot reach you." He means it more literally now than he did when Hardby was a rumour. A letter to Loftwick and back is the better part of two months.

A fourth idea

Caelith will hear a fourth idea if the party has one. A berth on a fast packet would beat the wool trader by a fortnight — and costs what a small manor costs, and packets carry the mails, which means a passenger list read by the harbour authority at both ends. He will price it honestly and let them decide; if they can find the money, let them have it, and let them learn what buying speed costs. Their own teleport magic he will not provide and is wary of — the Aerdi read magical arrivals, and he would rather they were slow than announced. He will advise against splitting up, on all three roads and at any speed: "You are stronger than my agents because you are together."

GM: whatever they choose, the journey is weeks, not days. Narrate it in a paragraph if the table wants to get on with it — but let the season turn while they ride, and let them arrive somewhere that has had time to change.

Trina, asked, says nothing about the first or third roads; of the second she says only, "Castrian's house is mine in everything but the address. He will know you are mine. Do not embarrass him."

Hand-off to the next chapter

The road the party chose sets the conditions the next chapter opens under. Price the choice; don't editorialize it — none of these is a failure.

Road takenHow long the firm has knownTamsin Moraven, in HardbyTheir Hardby contacts
Official Delegation (authority)~9 weeksConfirmed dead — a body recovered days before they arrive.Witnesses scattered; the broker moved upcountry; a paper trail only.
Commercial Cover (cover)~5 weeksAlive, moved to a coastal estate two days east — recoverable with effort.Veska Maelan and Castrian Vell both reachable; the broker confrontable.
Quiet Pursuit (distance)~2 weeksAlive, still in Hardby — held in a warehouse, a live rescue.Every contact unprepared and within reach; the broker easiest of all.

Ending Read-Aloud — Departing East

Read aloud at the moment the party leaves Loftwick under whichever travel approach they chose. The text below is approach-agnostic — it works whether they ride out at noon as a delegation or before dawn as nameless travelers. Adjust the small details (number of horses, presence of clerks, the form of farewell) to match.

Loftwick is at its quietest in the hour you leave. The Civic Way is broad and pale; the lamps along the Audit Hall still burn though the sky has gone the color of new milk. At the Little Palace gate the footmen raise their lanterns once and lower them — the old Yeomanry sign for safe travel.

Caelith stands at the gate. He embraces no one. He steps to the lead rider and offers a small flat brass token — the quill above the closed gate. "If you find the man who underwrote him, write to me at this house, with this on the seal. Three days from now I will be in this office, or its successor. The token will reach me either way."

Then a second thing, out of his coat: a folded letter, sealed, the wax unstamped. "For a trade-clearing notary in Hardby. Veska Maelan, on Whalemarket Quay. She has been my friend for twelve years and she has never seen one of your faces, so she will want the letter before she wants the faces. If the office is shut, or if she is not alone, do not push and do not wait in the street. Say this at her threshold instead, and say it once — a tower above three waves. If she is free to answer, she will say it back to you." A beat. "If she does not say it back, walk on and come again tomorrow. That is not a code. That is a woman telling you there is someone in the room."

And one thing more, unsealed, folded small: a folded slip in his own careful hand. He does not read it out. "An address in the Hardby merchants' quarter, the woman at the corner grocer who keeps the key, and what to say to her so that she stops asking. It is a widow's house with no widow in it. Do not open this at the gate — open it when Hardby is a day off, and read it to each other then."

Trina is at his shoulder. She has already said what she needed to say, last night, in private, to the last of you she walked with. The silver leaf at her collar catches the early light. She lifts a hand, and lowers it.

The road bends out of the Civic Way onto the poplar lane, and by the time the walls drop behind you the lamps of the Audit Hall have gone out. You ride an hour before anyone speaks, and when someone finally does, you find that none of you has yet asked the question you all carry: what was waiting for him in Rel Astra — and is it waiting still.

Where the next chapter picks up

Hardby is three weeks east on the post roads, six by sea with a wool trader, and ten behind a councilman's carriage and its paperwork. Rel Astra is further still, and Caelith does not say how much further, because he does not want them thinking past Hardby yet. The next chapter opens as they come into Hardby — at the West Gate under accreditation, at the South Gate off the post roads, or up the Whalemarket steps from a wool trader's deck, depending on the road they took.
